hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of k squared and a length of negative five k squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative four k with a length of negative five k squared.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{-5k^2}(k^2-4k)
\\\\
&=\goldE{-5k^2}(k^2)+(\goldE{-5k^2})(-4k)
\\\\
&=-5k^4+20k^3
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of k squared and a length of negative five k squared. Inside of this rectangle is negative five k to the fourth. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative four k with a length of negative five k squared. Inside of this rectangle is twenty k cubed.
